svg.title: NIGHTLY targets -- graded on a per-submission rerun

g.text: NIGHTLY targets -- graded on a per-submission rerun
Phase 1: on submission -- mark the work, grade nothing
Every task here has feedback_mode = NIGHTLY,
so the AI phase grades nothing and spends no
tokens. The tasks stay NEEDED, so
what puts this submission in tonight's queue.
Phase 2: nightly -- trigger a rerun per submission
The query does not mention feedback_mode. Any
task still NEEDED qualifies, which means an
IMMEDIATE target whose grading failed earlier
is retried tonight for free. Its feedback
arrives next morning rather than at once, a
Rerun is per submission, so the trigger only
Still the one fragile step: Gradescope has no
public API, so locating a submission and
clicking its rerun button is UI automation and
will break when they reskin. Keep every
Consider throttling the loop. A term's worth
of submissions clicked as fast as Playwright
manages looks like abuse from the outside.
Phase 3: the rerun -- grade the NIGHTLY tasks
reasons other than our nightly job: an
instructor debugging the autograder, a TA
re-running a flaky test. None should re-bill
[for each task with ai_needed and ai_status = PENDING]
Tasks already DONE from an earlier IMMEDIATE
pass are skipped by ai_status, so a
mixed-mode submission does not pay twice for
1. A failed task stays NEEDED and increments
attempt_count. The next night retries it
2. LLM calls retry with backoff on 429 and 5xx
3. If the trigger cannot find or click a
submission's rerun button, record it on
trigger_run and surface it. A silent trigger
